one_liner: Reference code for EGSR 2021 stochastic generation: Owen-scrambled Sobol', Halton, Faure and pmj02(bn) sequences at O(1) per coordinate.
what_it_does: The library fills a caller-provided double array (sample-major, n x nd) with a randomized low-discrepancy sequence: stochastic Sobol' (up to 64 dimensions), pmj02 (2D), stochastic Faure (0,3)/(0,5)/(0,7)/(0,11), or stochastic Halton (up to 10 dimensions). Options add progressive shuffling, best-candidate (blue-noise) placement in the first two dimensions, and full Owen scrambling instead of correlated swapping for Faure and Halton. The API is a set of free functions in sampling/*.h, such as GetStochasticSobolSamples(n, nd, shuffle, candidates, owen, out), plus a stateless GetSobolStateless(idx, dim, seed) for single coordinates. There are also generate_samples and shuffle_indices command-line tools. It is not a drop-in for anything: no other library is wrapped or replaced.
how_it_is_fast: Stochastic generation (Helmer, Christensen, Kensler, EGSR 2021) builds the scrambled sequence directly instead of generating Sobol' points and then Owen-scrambling them digit by digit. For each new index prev_len+i, each dimension looks up an earlier sample at i XOR a precomputed per-dimension 'xor-value', takes that sample's stratum, flips its last digit (stratum ^ 1, or a base-b digit add for Faure and Halton), and draws one uniform offset inside the flipped stratum. So each coordinate costs one table lookup, one array read and one PCG32 draw, and the output is distributed as an Owen-scrambled sequence. The stateless variant recurses over the index bits instead, at O(log n) per coordinate.
when_to_use: Monte Carlo or quasi-Monte Carlo integration (rendering, option pricing, uncertainty propagation) where you want Owen-scrambled Sobol', Faure or Halton points with fresh randomization per run.
Precomputing sample tables (pmj02, pmj02bn, ssobol) in a renderer or tool, where the whole array is generated at once.
Low-dimensional integrands of 3, 5, 7 or 11 dimensions at power-of-base sample counts: the sfaure (0,s)-sequences stratify on all elementary intervals.
Learning or reimplementing the paper: the code favours readability, and the README says a specialised 2D version (paper Listing 2) is about 3x faster.
when_not_to_use: You need plain uniform random numbers: this produces stratified point sets, not a PRNG stream; use a PRNG (std::mt19937 replacement) instead.
You need reproducible output: the array generators take no seed and seed PCG32 from std::random_device on each call; only the stateless Sobol' function takes a seed.
Per-sample on-the-fly generation inside a renderer: the main generators need the whole n x nd array resident because each point reads an earlier one, so streaming needs the slower stateless path.
More than 64 Sobol' or 10 Halton dimensions, or more than about 2^31 coordinates: dimensions are capped by compile-time tables, and indices and n*nd products are plain int.
Production use that needs error handling: bad arguments call std::terminate via an ASSERT macro, and there are no tests, releases or packaging.

integration.dependencies: none (C++ standard library only); xor_values.py (Python) is needed only to regenerate xor-value tables
integration.platforms: any; portable scalar C++ with no SIMD or intrinsics; 32-bit builds fixed by PR #1 (merged 2023-12-14)
integration.thread_safety: Not documented; each call builds its own RNG, and the seeding helper in rng.h uses thread_local engines, so concurrent calls on separate output arrays look independent (inferred from the source).

gotchas: Best-candidate mode (--bn2d, candidates > 1) evaluates kBestCandidateSamples = 100 candidates per point, with a grid nearest-neighbour query each, so pmj02bn-style output costs far more than plain pmj02 or ssobol.
The stateless Sobol' functions were broken until the 2022-09-01 commit 'Fix bugs with the stateless Sobol' implementation'; use current HEAD.

Progressive shuffling ASSERTs that the sample count is a constant multiple of a power of the base (otherwise std::terminate) and copies the full array. Halton cannot be shuffled, and passing owen=true to ssobol or pmj02 only prints a warning and is ignored.
Strata of earlier points are recovered by multiplying stored doubles by the stratum count, so outputs must stay as double; do not narrow the buffer to float.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: No quasi-random siblings are catalogued yet; every listed sibling (Randompack, OpenRAND, EigenRand, the xoshiro and PCG variants) is a pseudo-random generator for independent uniforms. Pick this when you need stratified, Owen-scrambled point sets for integration, and a sibling PRNG when you need a random stream.
verified_claims_summary: There are no measurements to verify. The README claims the code is 'faster than any other published method' for these sequences, names no competitor, and says the paper's 2D-only Listing 2 is about 3x faster. The paper abstract (WebSearch snippet only; the paper itself is egress-blocked) puts Listing 2 at 200 million samples/s on one CPU thread, which would imply roughly 65 million 2D samples/s for this library (derived, unmeasured, hardware unknown). For context, the author's earlier pmj-cpp documents pmj02 at about 1.65 million samples/s on a 2017 MacBook Pro, but that is different code and hardware.
status_note: Code has been stable since the 2023-12-14 32-bit fix (the 2026 commits only touch the README); MIT-licensed, about 1,700 lines of plain C++14 across sampling/, easy to vendor, with 55 stars and no open issues.
